idiom_name: Hash#dig / Hash#fetch(key, default) plus keyword-argument defaults in a from_hash constructor
implementation_notes: JSON.parse returns plain Hash and Array objects, so the reader is a small from_hash class method: fetch with a default for optional keys (fetch("x", 0)), dig for nested navigation, and keyword arguments with defaults in the constructor to express the same defaults once. Keys the reader never mentions are never touched, which is what makes the object tolerate producer additions without any library support. When the schema is complex or shared, dry-struct/dry-types or a Struct subclass with keyword_init can formalise the same reader.
pitfalls: Hash#dig returns nil for an absent key, an explicit null and a non-hash intermediate step alike, so presence cannot be inferred from the result; use key?/fetch when the distinction matters.
JSON.parse produces String keys unless symbolize_names: true is set, and the two are not interchangeable: a reader that expects symbols silently falls back to defaults for every field.
A Hash built with a mutable default (Hash.new([])) or a reader that mutates nested values aliases the parsed payload, so "reading" can change data other code still sees.
